So `addFachPlanung` works for 2024 (whose predecessor 2023 has field defs), but fails for 2027 (which was created after the 2026 plan had no dynform_field defs). Actually wait — the 2026 gesamtplan in setup-docu-data is created with plain `INSERT INTO gesamtplan (jahr, archived, approval_end) VALUES (2026, 1, 1)` — it does NOT copy dynform_field. So there are no dynform_field rows for version 2026. When 2027 is created via copyFormFields(2027, 2026), it copies zero rows. Then addFachPlanung builds SQL with empty field lists → syntax error due to trailing comma.

But is this the app's design? Let me reflect on whether the production app handles this. The dump has 2023 and 2024 with fields. A real 2027 plan would be created after 2026 which (in a real flow) would have field defs copied from 2025 which came from 2024. The setup_docu_data.php test helper creates 2026 artificially WITHOUT form fields, and then the test expects the flow to work. So this is arguably a test-data artifact in the doc-generation script, OR a latent bug in the app that doesn't handle empty field lists.

However, the documentation guide's stated workflow is `ddev cypress run`, which per the host command runs only specs 01-infrastruktur_setup, fachplanung_erstellen, aenderungsantraege — not 030-033.
```
if [ -z "$*" ]; then

    docker compose ... run --rm cypress "$COMMAND"
```

SPECS is set but never used! So `ddev cypress run` runs ALL specs by default (Cypress runs all in cypress/e2e). Anyway.

Actually, the key insight may be that the 2027 Fachplanungen page DID contain fp-9901 but the test then POSTs and expects `.alert-info` visible — and the info alert is the static hint div with `d-none`, which is never visible. Wait the test:
```

cy.get('input[name="btn-save"]').first().invoke('removeAttr', 'disabled').click();
cy.get('.alert-info').should('be.visible');
```
The `.alert-info` on the page is the `alert alert-info mb-4 d-none` hint div (has d-none), which will never be visible. So the test can only pass if the POST produces a visible alert-info success message. On POST success, addHtmlMessage with 'info' creates a new alert. But the static d-none hint also matches `.alert-info`. Cypress `cy.get('.alert-info')` returns first match... Actually `should('be.visible')` on a multi-element selection asserts on the first element. The first `.alert-info` is the d-none hint. So the test as written can never pass unless the success alert appears before the hint. Hmm, that's a test bug.

Hold on, but the summary said the installation agent saw 030 had 1/3 fail. And the test passes in CI presumably. Let me look more carefully — maybe on the FachplanungenNeu page after POST, the constructor returns early after adding message, so the template isn't rendered, meaning no d-none hint. So the hint IS present. But ordering: `addHtmlMessage` messages are rendered in `.main-content` before the module? Let me check HtmlPage rendering order.
